construction.note: This uses Manuel Martínez Vela’s published grid method and the photograph of the bones panel with grid and diagonals overlaid in ALZADA 115, page 45. We read the outlines and supplied the compass construction and step grouping.
construction.changes: The article explains the shared grid and shows the completed tracing. It does not give this pattern’s numbered app sequence. Its separate nine-step Partal example is a different pattern. Source credits identify the design and method, not a verbatim sequence.

credits.source: La Alhambra con regla y compás: el trazado de los diseños geométricos nazaríes (ALZADA 115, 2017)
credits.creator: Manuel Martínez Vela
credits.note: The article shows this Comares panel (“los huesos”) photographed with its grid and diagonals drawn over it; the outlines here were read from that photo.

photos.caption: The tiled panel of bones in the Salón de Embajadores (Comares), Alhambra, seen at an angle (cropped).
photos.creator: Jl FilpoC

given.O: The centre of a square where four bones meet.
given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is half a square of the grid.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A. Keep this compass size until the end. The distance OA is half a square of the grid.

Draw a circle with centre A through O. It crosses the line again at B. Draw a circle with centre B through A. It crosses the line again at C. Draw a circle with centre C through B. It crosses the line again at D. Draw the same three circles on the left of O, with centres E, F and G. They give F, G and H. E is where the first circle crosses the line on the left.

Draw a vertical line through O. It crosses the first circle at J and N. Draw a circle with centre J through O. It crosses the vertical line again at K. Draw a circle with centre K through J. It crosses it again at L. Draw a circle with centre L through K. It crosses it again at M. Draw the same three circles below O, with centres N, P and Q. They give P, Q and R.
Draw a vertical line through each of G, E, A and C. Draw a horizontal line through each of Q, N, J and L. The lines make a square grid, with O in the middle of a square.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a vertical line through E. Draw a vertical line through A. Draw a horizontal line through N. Draw a horizontal line through J. The four lines make a square with O in its middle.

steps.text: Draw the line through O that halves the angle AOJ. Draw the line through O that halves the angle JOE. Draw two lines through each of H, F, B and D, parallel to these two lines. Every square of the grid now has both its diagonals.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw the line through O that halves the angle AOJ. Draw the line through O that halves the angle JOE. Draw two lines through H, parallel to these two lines. Draw two lines through D, parallel to these two lines.

steps.text: Join D, M, H and R to mark the tile that repeats. It stands on a corner, two squares from O each way.

ink.text: Ink the outline of the bones. Each bone is three squares long. At both ends it reaches out along the diagonals, like a bone with knobbed ends.

parts.text: Ink from S8 to S2, through O. Ink from S2 to S1, then from S1 to D. Ink from M to S3.
Ink the same lines turned round O, three more times. Tick “Also ink the copies round the centre” to ink them all at once.

pattern.text: Put copies of the tile side by side. Upright and lying bones interlock like a basket weave. In the Hall of Comares the upright bones are black, green and ochre. The lying ones are white.

expect.note: Golden values in units of OA (half a grid square, so one square is 4); every piece is the same bone of 4 squares, two per tile of 8 squares.
